content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository pulp-platform_common_cells_pr222, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# `stream_arbiter` with priority arbitration inherently violates assertion
When configuring a `stream_arbiter` or `stream_arbiter_flushable` with `ARBITER = "prio"`, it instantiates an `rr_arb_tree` with both the `ExtPrio` and `LockIn` parameters set:
https://github.com/pulp-platform/common_cells/blob/0d67563b6b592549542544f1abc0f43e5d4ee8b4/src/stream_arbiter_flushable.sv#L55-L61
However, this directly violates an assertion in `rr_arb_tree`:
https://github.com/pulp-platform/common_cells/blob/0d67563b6b592549542544f1abc0f43e5d4ee8b4/src/rr_arb_tree.sv#L319
As a result, any priority stream arbiters instantiated inherently cause a fatal assertion violation.

<analysis>
The core of the problem is that in the “prio” case we are instantiating rr_arb_tree with both ExtPrio=1 and LockIn=1.  rr_arb_tree’s internal assertion (at its own line 319) explicitly forbids LockIn when ExtPrio is enabled, so every priority-arbiter instantiation immediately fails.  To resolve this, we must:

1. In the “prio” instantiation, change LockIn to 0 (or otherwise parameterize it off ExtPrio).
2. Audit the “rr” instantiation to ensure its parameters remain correct (ExtPrio=0, LockIn=1) and update comments/documentation so the distinction is clear.
3. Optionally introduce a localparam or helper logic near the module parameters to derive LockIn from ARBITER, thereby avoiding the mismatch in the future.
4. Mirror the same fix in the non-flushable stream_arbiter (not shown here) so both variants stay consistent.

Below are three critical locations in src/stream_arbiter_flushable.sv that require inspection or edits to implement these fixes.
